answer_text: Textbooks often use diagrams and free-body illustrations to explain this kind of concept. This is a foundational concept in physics. An object floats or sinks depending on how its density compares to water: if the object is less dense than water, the buoyant force pushes it up and it floats; if denser, it sinks. Wood floats because it is less dense than water, while a steel nail sinks because it is denser. This is one of the fundamental laws typically covered early in a physics course.
